svg.aria-label: BodyCount’s features, in eleven animated screens, each with its mechanism. Biometric lock: the fingerprint scanned, the key leaves the Keystore, HKDF derives the database key and the vault key, and the people list fills in. People: “vann” typed in the search, the query is rewritten on every letter and goes from 18 to 7 people, the cards slide, then Top rated reorders them. Statistics: the year’s 78 encounters each fall into their month, the bars rise, +136% against 2025, the podium sorts itself. Map of France: the real coastline read from france.bin, the cities drop in as bubbles with their ripples and shuttles, and a pinch splits the 65 bubble into Vannes 61 and Auray 4. Calendar: busy days take their disc and their signs, the 23rd is touched and its six signs get sorted, three remain. Private gallery: a photo picked in the system picker goes into the vault, blurs, encrypted with AES-GCM, the copy is deleted, nothing in the phone’s gallery, then it is decrypted in memory for the viewer. Backup: the passphrase, PBKDF2 over 210,000 rounds, then the BCEX2 file written chunk by chunk. What it brings in: seven paid nights out of 78 light up, €750 in total, €107.14 on average over paid ones only. Nothing is final: an encounter reopened, its rating corrected, a deletion asked then cancelled. Address and route: only the address goes through the door, to the map app you pick, which draws the route in the real Gulf of Morbihan. Three screen sizes: the same people list in 2, 3 then 4 columns. And nothing leaves: no server, no account, no telemetry.

svg.text: Eleven screens, each with its mechanism. Everything happens on the phone, and nowhere else.

g.text: The fingerprint brings the key into memory. Without it, nothing reads.
Every letter reruns the query, the sorts reorder.
Each encounter falls into its month, the podium sorts itself.
The real coastline, built in. Moving closer splits the cities.
Seven columns, and under each day its rarest signs.
A photo enters the vault encrypted, never the gallery.
Everything in one file, locked by your passphrase.
An amount per night, the average over paid ones only.
Edit, correct, delete, or change your mind.
The only way out of the phone, and on a tap.
The same list, in 2, 3 then 4 columns.
Everything stays on this device. No account,
Encrypted database, key kept in the Keystore

g.text: Only it will read it back.
The average only counts paid ones.
Empty means nothing: not a €0 night.
It leaves the statistics, the map and
the calendar. The notes written that
Another app: it knows where you go.
authenticate(): Android checks the finger, the app never sees it.
unlock(): the key leaves the Keystore-encrypted preferences.
HKDF derives two keys: one never gives away the other.
The database opens, then the vault: the faces arrive.
FROM personnes p LEFT JOIN rencontres r
Every letter reruns a single query on the encrypted database.
The remaining people slide into place.
A sort only changes the order of the same query.
Search, city and tags add up: each filter narrows, nothing is read on its own.
SELECT strftime('%m', quand) AS mois, COUNT(*) FROM rencontres GROUP BY mois
Each encounter falls into its month: the database counts, the app draws.
The podium: the average rating, then the number of times.
the opening view, over all of France
From the main one, nearest first,
up to two thirds of the encounters.
Two disks that touch make one bubble
gap 15 pt < 41 pt: a single bubble, 65
back to 4.3×: the bubble closes again
The disks never move by a single point:
moving closer is what splits them.
The real coastline, read from france.bin: not one tile, not one request.
Two ripples on the main city, a shuttle to every other.
A pinch on the gulf: the 65 bubble splits.
The zoom button brings back the opening view.
The days fill in. Touch a day: its signs get sorted.
Wednesday 23: six signs apply, three fit under the disc.

g.text: Every busy day gets its disc, and its rarest signs below.
All drawn from what is already entered: nothing extra to fill in.
Android hands over a copy in the clear: it only passes through.
Encrypted on arrival, under a meaningless name, then the copy deleted.
To show it, decrypted in memory, never on disk.
in the clear: the mark and the salt
encrypted in one-megabyte chunks: the cards, then every photo and video
one megabyte at most, even for a 200 MB video
A passphrase, not the phone’s key: the file travels.
The file is written as a stream, each media out of the vault and re-encrypted.
Saved where you want; the date noted quiets the reminder for a month.
An amount per encounter, in cents: most have none.
The average only counts paid nights.
A field left empty means nothing, not a night worth zero.
Touching an encounter reopens it as it was: correct, save.
Saving rereads the card, the statistics, the map and the calendar.
Deleting always asks, and says what will go.
the one you pick, and only it
the rest of the card stays in
Everything entered stays in the encrypted database.
A tap on “Go there”: only the address goes through the door.
The map app works out the route, BodyCount knows nothing of it.
The number to the dialer, the backup where you save it: the other doors work the same way.
On 16:9, two columns, the search under the title.
On the Fold’s cover, wide and short: three columns.
Unfolded, a rail on the left and four columns: the layout follows.

svg.text: Each one has its own diagram further down, showing it in detail.
